analysis_trace: Trial NCT06791733 is a randomized crossover study investigating inter-set passive static stretching effects on muscle performance in healthy resistance-trained men. Three arms: AG (agonist stretching), AN (antagonist stretching), CG (control/no stretching). Primary endpoint: total volume across sessions. Secondary endpoints: strength (Newtons), power (Watts), velocity (m/s) via T-Force device.

Evidence review: Padilha et al. (2019, PMC6926438) found inter-set agonist stretching reduced total work and increased fatigue index vs control, suggesting AG may impair acute performance. Schoenfeld et al. (2022, Frontiers) reviewed inter-set stretch for hypertrophy but noted limited evidence for acute performance enhancement. Bahrami et al. (2025, PMC11877292) found antagonist stretching did not significantly influence agonist performance, with trivial effects.

Evidence-role mapping: Padilha - direct_numeric for AG impairment (work -15-20%, fatigue +25%); Bahrami - direct_numeric for AN (trivial effect, d≈0.2); Schoenfeld - mechanism_background for hypertrophy signaling.

Population match: healthy resistance-trained men, matching inclusion criteria. Endpoint match: total volume, strength, power, velocity measures align. Timepoint: 2-week crossover matches acute/chronic ambiguity.

Key uncertainty: Limited direct evidence for antagonist stretching on chest press performance; T-Force device validity established but population-specific responses unclear. Crossover design mitigates inter-individual variance but order effects possible.

Prediction rationale: AG likely impairs total volume vs CG based on Padilha. AN may preserve or slightly enhance volume vs CG based on antagonist co-contraction reduction theory, though Bahrami showed null effects. Secondary endpoints follow volume patterns with strength/power/velocity correlated to neuromuscular fatigue.
